measures.what_it_does: Restores Lopez Island Fire & EMS's regular property tax to $0.74 per $1,000 for 2027 collection, up from about $0.47 after years of the 1% limit, and lets the levy grow up to 3% a year instead of 1% through 2035. The district says the money maintains current fire, EMS and firefighter-safety levels. Majority vote.
measures.cost_line: $0.74 per $1,000 in 2027, up from $0.476 in 2025: about $370 a year on a $500,000 property instead of $238. Up to 3% yearly growth follows through 2035.
measures.pro_summary: Jim Ghiglione: 12 years since the last fire levy; the district has stretched its money with loans, used vehicles, grants and insurance billing, and needs the levy and a 3% factor to keep up with inflation.
measures.con_summary: No statement against was filed; the pamphlet says no volunteers came forward.

taxes.basis: A yes vote raises the district's regular levy rate by more than half, from about $0.47 to $0.74 per $1,000, and replaces the 1% growth limit with up to 3% for nine years. It stays under the $1.50 cap and the $0.83 voters approved in 2013, the case for +1.

measures.sources_note: Sources: the San Juan County voters' pamphlet, pages 50-51 (S1); VoteWA record 7286 (S2); the county's Current Election page (S3); DOR 2025 levy detail (S4); RCW 84.55.050 (S5); DOR and county GIS (S6).

measures.what_it_does: Lengthens Port of Lopez commissioners' terms from four years to six for commissioners elected after the vote; sitting commissioners keep their terms. One of the three seats would then be up every other cycle instead of two at once every fourth year.
measures.cost_line: No tax. The port says six-year terms would lower its election costs; no figure is given.
measures.pro_summary: Wil Catlin and Kenn Aufderhar: most Washington ports have six-year terms; four-year terms put two-thirds of the commission up at once, hurting stability and doubling election costs that cycle.
measures.con_summary: No statement against was filed; the Auditor sought writers and none came forward.
measures.sources_note: Sources: the San Juan County voters' pamphlet, pages 52-53 (S1); VoteWA record 7287 (S2); the Auditor's call for opposing writers (S3); RCW 53.12.172 and 53.12.175 (S4); SOS precinct results (S5). No rubric axis applies to a change in term length.

measures.what_it_does: Renews the Orcas Island Park and Recreation District's property tax for six years at $0.15 per $1,000, to fund programs, services and facilities such as Buck Park. The district must seek voter approval every six years. Needs 60% approval and minimum turnout.
measures.cost_line: $0.15 per $1,000 for 2027 collection, for six years: about $120 a year on an $800,000 home. The district collected $0.103 per $1,000 in 2025, about $82 on the same home.
measures.pro_summary: Ed Andrews, Jason Bradshaw and Barb Skotte: a renewal, not a new tax, for a district serving up to 3,000 islanders a year; failure means cuts, deferred maintenance and fewer programs.
measures.con_summary: Nathan Carter: programs are better funded by grants, endowments and volunteers; a standard levy burdens residents regardless of circumstances; the district could seek a narrower budgeted levy instead.

taxes.basis: A yes vote renews an existing six-year property tax at $0.15 per $1,000, above the $0.103 collected in 2025 because the 1% limit eroded the old rate. A renewal of a small levy maps 1; the rate increase is the case for 2.

measures.sources_note: Sources: the San Juan County voters' pamphlet, pages 54-55 (S1); VoteWA record 7288 (S2); DOR 2025 levy detail (S3); theOrcasonian on the district's 2010 levy (S4); SOS precinct results (S5); DOR GIS (S6).

measures.what_it_does: A one-year excess property tax of $210,000 for 2027 to run the Lopez Island dump (garbage disposal, free recycling, Take It Or Leave It) and fund capital improvements. Disposal districts can levy only one year at a time, so the district asks every year. Needs 60% approval.
measures.cost_line: $210,000 for 2027, about $0.091 per $1,000: roughly $45.50 on a $500,000 property, the same amount as the current levy.
measures.pro_summary: Clauda Costa, Mehgan Alexandra and Carey Chenoweth: the levy is one of several recurring supports, with fees, recyclables and volunteers, that keep current services and free recycling going.
measures.con_summary: No statement against was filed; the Auditor sought writers and none came forward.

taxes.basis: A yes vote renews a one-year excess property tax at the same $210,000 as the current levy, about $0.09 per $1,000. A same-amount renewal of a small levy maps 1.

measures.sources_note: Sources: the San Juan County voters' pamphlet, pages 56-57 (S1); VoteWA record 7285 (S2); the district's levy explainer and history (S3, S4); DOR 2025 levy detail (S5); SOS precinct results, 2020-2025 (S6); the Auditor's call for opposing writers (S7).
